parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is high-risk. National passport/visa rules force birth-sex data and allow refusal or fraud findings where sex is doubted; the state/province explicitly restricts gender-congruent bathrooms in many government buildings. National immigration/prison reports document abusive placement and coerced therapy; local school-care and pronoun-disclosure rules worsen risk for minors. There is no documented effective visitor remedy or targeted anti-trans violence pattern; some protections exist but do not neutralize institutional exclusion. Score reflects universal document/facility exposure with severe possible consequences, moderated by mixed acceptance and contested legalism.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports are restricted to assigned-sex markers and X-marker issuance stopped. Visa cable instructs refusal or evidence requests when documents/records cast doubt on sex; suspected wilful misrepresentation may trigger fraud and lifetime ineligibility. Reports include passports blocked/confiscated and travellers detained over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; litigation and legal-aid guidance continue, but Supreme Court allowed marker restrictions, so operative visitor protection is limited.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening can escalate into detention, questioning, or inability to use congruent facilities if a traveller’s appearance conflicts with records.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy policies. A parent-framework arrest example shows trans detainee held in men’s ward. Local visitor detention protocol not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented visitor-facing custody safeguard; national hate-crime statute can address external violence but not institutional custody practices.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visa fraud or facility trespass allegation could move a traveller into questioning, refusal or custody where birth-sex placement rules apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National rules bar trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. The state/province law explicitly restricts gender-congruent bathroom use in many state-run facilities; national map notes criminal trespass in some states and documents a bathroom arrest. Local criminal enforcement is not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Bans are not universal in this state/province’s described scope, and city/hate-crime/employment floors exist; no documented local visitor-access remedy.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Staff checks at government buildings, schools, courts or public transport could trigger removal, refusal, questioning or arrest under facility rules.

care_services.exposure: Local gender-affirming care to minors is illegal; national rules threaten youth-care reimbursement and criminalize school facilitation. State pronoun-disclosure rules affect minors. Visitor emergency-care and medication practice are not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor’s medical, school or public-building visit can intersect with document checks, facility placement and caregiver refusal.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders define sex at birth, remove gender language, criminalize school pronoun facilitation and frame radical gender ideology in counterterrorism; local law restricts bathrooms, pronoun accommodations and sports. A parent bathroom arrest shows enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime and employment protection, some city safeguards, courts blocking/enjoining several orders, and state support for anti-discrimination moderate street hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing increases suspicion in document and facility checks and weakens reporting confidence.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor visitor may be barred from care, excluded from congruent facilities, and subject to school pronoun-disclosure rules; guardians may encounter refusal, questioning or custody if documents mismatch. Adult-only risks remain document/facility based.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family visits to schools, clinics or government buildings can trigger disclosure, service refusal or entry/care complications.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated local anti-trans violence incidents are documented. Public hostility exists, but routine raids, gang sweeps or police targeting of travellers are not established.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute, city protections and mixed acceptance signal possible recourse, but no documented local bias-crime statute or effective response record.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence risk is not the driver; institutional document/facility hostility can worsen reporting and response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented effective remedy for passport/entry sex-doubt, state facility exclusion, minor-care refusal or visitor custody placement. Several national orders are blocked, enjoined or in litigation, but current enforcement status varies.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, civil-liberties suit, hate-crime/employment law and court injunctions create partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Travelers may face overlapping document, facility and care checks before any remedy becomes available.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable to 0.35-A in birth-sex facility exclusion and limited remedies, but lower because national/visa document screening, fraud grounds, immigration custody abuse and minor-care bans add severe exposure. It lacks 0.35-A's emergency-ward detail and private-hotel mitigation but carries stronger state-level institutional hostility.

Above 0.25-D because there is no documented all-facility compulsory birth-sex rule, invasive hospital placements, routine police fraud stops or systematic raids. Yet the state’s explicit facility restriction and national entry screening keep it materially below elevated-risk anchors that lack such legal exclusions.

Far above 0.15-D: no registry, checkpoint disclosure, mandatory registration or routine detention/fraud sentencing of trans travellers is documented. The risk is institutional exclusion and possible custody, not engineered universal discovery and near-automatic severe punishment.

parsed.synthesis: The national and state/province rules interact: visa/passport sex checks create entry exposure; local facility bans turn public-building use into document/identity scrutiny; arrest or visa-fraud allegations could lead into custody where reported birth-sex placement, care denial and abuse apply. Minor travel adds school-care and pronoun-disclosure pressure. Social acceptance and court injunctions reduce private-violence certainty but do not offset unremedied institutional exclusion, so the operative regime sits in high risk.
